encounters.cc: Irregular menstrual cycles and worsening facial hair.

lines: Irregular menstrual cycles and worsening facial hair.
She reports having only 5–6 periods per year since menarche at age 12.
Over the past 18 months, she has also noticed increased dark hair growth on her chin and around her nipples, which she finds embarrassing.
She denies vision problems, galactorrhea, or recent illness.
- Medroxyprogesterone acetate 10 mg orally daily for 10 days monthly (cyclic)
- Prenatal vitamin with folate 1 tablet orally daily
- Mother: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, diagnosed age 45
- Maternal aunt: Endometrial cancer, diagnosed age 52
On physical examination, she has moderate acne on her face, coarse terminal hair along the jawline and lower abdomen, and no clitoromegaly.
A urine pregnancy test is negative.
TSH and prolactin levels are normal.
Transvaginal ultrasound shows bilaterally enlarged ovaries with multiple small, peripherally arranged follicles.
The physician suspects a chronic endocrinologic condition associated with anovulation.

encounters.cc: Irregular menstrual cycles and difficulty conceiving.

lines: Irregular menstrual cycles and difficulty conceiving.
The patient returns one year after her initial visit for irregular menses and facial hair, presenting with continued menstrual irregularity and fertility concerns.
She reports infrequent periods since adolescence, currently menstruating every 6 to 8 weeks.
Over the past year, she has noticed increased hair growth on her chin and around her navel.
She denies headaches, visual disturbances, or galactorrhea, and remains concerned about long-term effects on fertility and endometrial health.
- Medroxyprogesterone acetate 10 mg orally daily for 10 days monthly (cyclic)
- Prenatal vitamin with folate 1 tablet orally daily
- Mother: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, diagnosed age 45
- Maternal aunt: Endometrial cancer, diagnosed age 52
On physical examination, she has terminal hairs along the chin and lower abdomen, and moderate acne across her cheeks and jawline.
A urine pregnancy test is negative.
Lab tests show normal prolactin and TSH levels.
Serum testosterone is mildly elevated, and the LH/FSH ratio is greater than 2:1.
Transvaginal ultrasound reveals bilaterally enlarged ovaries with multiple small follicles located peripherally.

encounters.cc: Irregular periods with heavy and prolonged bleeding.

lines: Irregular periods with heavy and prolonged bleeding.

The patient returns for evaluation of persistent menstrual irregularities in the context of polycystic ovary syndrome initially diagnosed in 2020, having previously presented for irregular cycles with facial hair in 2020 and difficulty conceiving in 2021.
She reports that over the past several years, her menstrual cycles have occurred every 1 to 2 months, often skipping months entirely.
When menses do occur, they are heavy and sometimes prolonged.
She also complains of increased hair growth on her chin and lower abdomen.
She denies headaches, galactorrhea, or visual disturbances.
She is not trying to get pregnant at this time.
- Medroxyprogesterone acetate 10 mg orally daily for 10 days monthly (cyclic)
- Prenatal vitamin with folate 1 tablet orally daily
- Mother: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, diagnosed age 45
- Maternal aunt: Endometrial cancer, diagnosed age 52
Physical examination shows moderate acne along the jawline and coarse hair over the upper lip and around the umbilicus.
Laboratory evaluation shows normal TSH and prolactin levels, elevated LH relative to FSH, and a serum testosterone level at the upper limit of normal.
Transvaginal ultrasound reveals bilaterally enlarged ovaries with multiple small follicles aligned peripherally.
The patient is started on a treatment plan focused on cycle regulation and reducing androgenic symptoms.

encounters.cc: Concerns about menstrual cycle irregularity while attempting to conceive for over a year.

lines: Concerns about menstrual cycle irregularity while attempting to conceive for over a year.
The patient returns for ongoing surveillance of endometrial hyperplasia and continued management of menstrual irregularities associated with polycystic ovary syndrome.
She presents with ongoing concerns regarding fertility.
She reports having a period only every 2–3 months for the past several years.
When she does menstruate, the bleeding is often heavy and prolonged.
She also notes increased facial hair and acne that have worsened in the last year.
She and her partner have been trying to conceive for over a year without success.
She denies headaches, visual changes, or galactorrhea.
- Medroxyprogesterone acetate 10 mg orally daily for 10 days monthly (cyclic)
- Prenatal vitamin with folate 1 tablet orally daily
- Mother: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, diagnosed age 45
- Maternal aunt: Endometrial cancer, diagnosed age 52
On physical examination, she has terminal hair on the upper lip and chin, as well as moderate acne on her cheeks.
A urine pregnancy test is negative.
Labs show mildly elevated serum testosterone, normal prolactin and TSH, and an increased LH/FSH ratio.
Transvaginal ultrasound shows bilaterally enlarged ovaries with multiple small follicles arranged along the periphery.
The patient is diagnosed with an endocrinologic condition contributing to anovulation.

encounters.cc: Concerns about irregular menstrual cycles with heavy prolonged menses and worsening acne.

lines: Concerns about irregular menstrual cycles with heavy prolonged menses and worsening acne.
The patient is a 33-year-old female with a history of polycystic ovary syndrome and endometrial hyperplasia without atypia who returns for management of menstrual irregularity.
She reports having only 4 to 5 periods per year for the past several years, often preceded by bloating and mood changes.
When menses occur, they are heavy and last over a week.
She notes increased facial hair and acne that have gradually worsened over the past year.
She denies headaches, nipple discharge, or visual changes.
- Medroxyprogesterone acetate 10 mg orally daily for 10 days monthly (cyclic)
- Prenatal vitamin with folate 1 tablet orally daily
- Mother: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, diagnosed age 45
- Maternal aunt: Endometrial cancer, diagnosed age 52
She is not sexually active and is not trying to conceive.
Physical examination reveals moderate hirsutism and acne, and pelvic examination is normal.
A urine pregnancy test is negative.
Laboratory tests show normal TSH and prolactin levels, elevated LH relative to FSH, and a total testosterone level at the upper limit of normal.
Pelvic ultrasound reveals bilaterally enlarged ovaries with multiple small follicles along the periphery.
